exam_scheme.note: The National Aptitude Test in Architecture (NATA) is conducted by the Council of Architecture (CoA), a statutory body constituted under the Architects Act, 1972, as the mandatory entrance assessment for admission to the first year of 5-year Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch) degree programmes across recognized government, aided, and private architecture colleges in India. The test carries a total of 200 marks and has a duration of 180 minutes (3 hours). The examination is divided into two distinct parts: Part A is a paper-based offline Drawing and Composition Test (3 questions, 80 marks: A1 Composition and Color 25 marks, A2 Sketching/Black and White 25 marks, A3 3D Composition 30 marks) administered for 90 minutes; and Part B is an online Computer Based Test (45 questions, 120 marks: Visual Reasoning, Logical Derivation, General Architecture Awareness, and Language Interpretation) administered for 90 minutes. Qualifying score requirement: Minimum qualifying marks in Part A, Part B, and an overall aggregate cutoff of 70 marks out of 200.

papers.paper_name: Part A: Drawing & Visual Composition Test (Offline Pen & Paper / Drawing Sheet)
papers.negative_marking: No negative marking (manual evaluation on color harmony, proportions, perspective)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum qualifying cutoff prescribed by CoA (typically 20 marks out of 80)

papers.paper_name: Part B: Online Computer Based Test (Visual Reasoning, Architecture Knowledge, Design Aptitude)
papers.negative_marking: No negative marking (+1, +2, or +3 marks depending on question type: MCQ, MSQ, PCQ)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum qualifying cutoff prescribed by CoA (typically 30 marks out of 120)
